thread:
sarah: acme-inc reported mobile TLS failures after last night's scheduled cert rotation (02:00 UTC). iOS clients behind certain carriers show handshake failures.
juan: can you paste the exact client error? any server logs?
acme-support: mobile logs: "TLSHandshakeFailed" and server side: "SSL: certificate verify failed". curl from their app server works.
sarah: reproduction is intermittent — some users connect fine, others always fail.
nina: curious — that often points at chain ordering or a truncated PEM. did rotator change how the bundle was concatenated?
rotator-bot: rotation job 672 completed at 2024-06-08T02:00:07Z, bundle 5258 bytes, intermediate included.
juan: can we get an `openssl s_client -connect` from outside their carrier NAT and from inside (if they can)? command: `openssl s_client -connect api.acme.example:443 -showcerts -servername api.acme.example`
acme-support: ran the command from their staging host (AWS) and attached output. shows 2 certs but order looks odd: leaf then root then intermediate.
nina: that ordering will break some TLS stacks (esp iOS) which expect leaf->intermediate->root. but ordering alone usually isn't intermittent. any chance the edge proxy is rewriting files on reload?
sarah: customer says they run a vendor edge proxy (managed) and do hot reload after we push certs.
juan: two more checks: `file cert_bundle.pem` and `hexdump -C cert_bundle.pem | sed -n '1,50p'` — looking for CRLF (0d 0a) vs LF (0a). some concat scripts accidentally leave `\r` bytes which cause downstream parsers to drop the last cert.
acme-support: ran `file` -> "ASCII text, with CRLF line terminators". hexdump shows `0d 0a` at boundaries.
nina: there we go. certain proxy implementations treat `\r\n` pairs in PEM concatenation poorly and on reload will truncate after an intermediate if the trailing `\r` is present. iOS clients (and some carrier middleboxes) are sensitive to strict DER parsing during handshake.
juan: quick repro: create two cert files with CRLF endings, concat with `cat a.crt b.crt > bundle.pem` and `openssl s_client -showcerts` against a simple server that uses the bundle — some clients will only receive two certs.
sarah: mitigation for customer: 1) canonicalize line endings on the bundle before uploading: `tr -d '\r' < bundle.pem > bundle.fixed.pem` 2) trigger a full restart of the edge proxy rather than hot reload to ensure it re-reads the file.
acme-support: applied `tr -d '\r'` and restarted the vendor proxy. iOS users who previously failed are now connecting. :tada:
juan: follow-ups: 1) we should add a validation step in the rotator pipeline to normalize endings and check `openssl verify` against the concatenated bundle. 2) add a content-length/bundle-size delta alert to detect odd truncation during upload.
nina: agreed. I'll open an ENG-PLATFORM task to patch the rotator and add a quick `openssl x509 -in bundle.fixed.pem -text -noout` check + `file` detection.
rotator-bot: creating ticket ROT-789 (normalize PEM endings + validate chain).
sarah: thx everyone. leaving a note for acct mgr to follow up with acme on vendor restart guidance.
acme-support: we'll schedule a short postmortem with the vendor to ensure their reload path preserves complete chain.
juan: logging action items: `#1 patch rotator (nina)`, `#2 add upload validation (eng)`, `#3 recommend full restart for vendors until patch lands (support)`.
sarah: closing thread — customer confirmed full recovery and we have a follow-up ticket. :white_check_mark:
